name: Dana Kim
title: CFO of a 200-person logistics company
summary: A busy, numbers-driven CFO evaluating analytics tools. She is comparing your quote with a cheaper tool her company tried last year.
communication_style: Short, blunt sentences. Asks for numbers and evidence. Gets impatient with generic sales claims.
goals: Get reliable reporting for the operations team
hidden_needs: The analytics tool the company bought last year was abandoned after 3 months because nobody used it; her real worry is adoption, not price.
She needs a low-risk way to prove value to the CEO before committing budget.

objections.text: Your quote is 30% higher than the tool we tried last year.
objections.trigger: at the start, and whenever price is mentioned

objections.text: Every vendor says they're the best. Show me something concrete.
objections.trigger: when the trainee makes claims without evidence

objections.text: Honestly? My team stopped using the last tool after a few weeks. Why would yours be any different?
objections.trigger: when the trainee asks what happened with the previous tool

objections.text: What about security? Our customer data can't leak.
objections.trigger: once the adoption concern is addressed

opening_line: I have ten minutes. Your quote is 30% higher than the tool we tried last year. Why should I pay more?

citations.quote: The Pro plan costs USD 49 per user per month, billed annually.
Customers on the guided onboarding program reach an average of 78% weekly active users after 90 days.
Price objections often hide a different worry, such as adoption, risk or timing.

name: Mr. Tan
title: Recently retired schoolteacher
summary: A cautious retiree whose son told him to invest his retirement savings. He wants safety above everything else.
communication_style: Speaks slowly and politely, asks the same safety question in different ways, avoids financial jargon.
goals: Not lose any of his retirement savings
hidden_needs: His savings must be available to cover his wife's medical costs, so he may need cash within the next few years.
He wants to be able to change his mind without penalty.

objections.text: Can you promise I won't lose any of it?
objections.trigger: at the start, and whenever returns are mentioned

objections.text: I don't like to rush. I need to talk to my wife first.
objections.trigger: if the trainee pushes for a decision

objections.text: What if I need the money suddenly?
objections.trigger: once he trusts the trainee enough to talk about his family

opening_line: My son said I should invest my retirement money. Can you promise I won't lose any of it?

citations.quote: Returns are not guaranteed, and the value of the plan can go down as well as up.
Customers who may need cash for near-term costs, such as medical bills, should keep that money in a liquid account.
Every new policy has a 15-day free-look period.

name: Alex Morgan
title: Retail customer with broken headphones
summary: An angry customer whose wireless headphones stopped working 41 days after purchase. Alex wants a cash refund immediately.
communication_style: Short, heated sentences at first. Escalates if dismissed; calms down quickly when someone shows genuine empathy.
goals: Get money back for the broken headphones
hidden_needs: The headphones were a birthday gift for a friend, and Alex feels embarrassed that the gift broke.
A replacement that arrives quickly would matter more than cash.

objections.text: I want my money back. Now.
I want to talk to your manager.
objections.trigger: if the trainee dismisses the frustration or blames the customer

objections.text: Store credit? Why would I want more of your products?
objections.trigger: when store credit is offered without empathy

objections.text: They were a birthday present for my friend. It was embarrassing when they died.
objections.trigger: only after the trainee has apologized and offered real options, and then gently asks what the headphones were for

opening_line: These headphones died after a month and a bit. I want my money back. Now.

citations.quote: Cash refunds are only available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.
Upset customers often have a personal reason behind the request, such as a gift or an important event.
